papers.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable
papers.abstract: Abstract  The capability of a modern AI agent depends not only on its foundation model but also on its harness, which constructs prompts, manages state, invokes tools, and coordinates execution. As models, APIs, environments, and requirements evolve, the harness must be continually modified. Before such a change can be made, a developer or coding agent must identify all code locations that implement the target behavior. This is difficult because production harnesses are large, tightly coupled, and behaviorally distributed, while modification requests describe what the system should do and repositories are organized by files and modules. Code search, repository indexing, and long-context processing ease inspection, but still leave this behavior-to-code mapping to be recovered by hand. Behavior localization is therefore a central bottleneck in harness evolution. We introduce the Harness Handbook, a behavior-centric representation synthesized automatically from a harness codebase via static analysis and LLM-assisted structuring, linking each behavior to its corresponding source. We also introduce Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD), which guides agents from high-level behaviors to relevant implementation details and verifies candidate locations against the current source. On diverse modification requests from two open-source harnesses, Handbook-Assisted planning improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality while using fewer planner tokens, with the largest gains on scattered sites, rarely executed paths, and cross-module interactions. Evolving complex agentic systems thus depends not only on generating edits, but also on determining where those edits should be made.

ru.title: Эволюция AI-агентов: от поведения к реализации
ru.desc: Статья рассматривает важность эволюции инструментов для современных AI-агентов, включающих фреймворки и модели. Для правильно управления поведением системы необходимо выявить все места в коде, которые реализуют цель поведения, что является сложной задачей из-за большой связанности и распределенности кода. Вводится 'Harness Handbook' — представление, автоматизированное с помощью статического анализа и LLM, которое связывает поведение с его источниками. Также предлагается метод BGPD, который направляет разработчиков от высокоуровневого поведения к деталям реализации.

en.title: Streamlining AI Harness Evolution with Behavior-Centric Tools
en.desc: This paper discusses the importance of a harness in AI systems, which manages prompts and execution as models and requirements change. It highlights the challenge of locating code that implements specific behaviors in large and complex codebases. The authors introduce the Harness Handbook, a tool that uses static analysis and LLMs to link behaviors to their source code. Additionally, they present Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD) to help developers navigate from high-level behaviors to implementation details, improving the efficiency of code modifications.

papers.title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce Boogu-Image-0.1, an open-source unified multimodal understanding and generation model family, comprising Base, Turbo, Edit, and Edit-Turbo variants. It delivers competitive performance in high-quality text-to-image generation, fast inference, instruction-based editing, and bilingual (Chinese-English) text rendering. Closed-source multimodal systems like Nano-Banana-Pro and GPT-Image-2 achieve strong performance through system-level integration rather than a single model, yet their internal practices remain largely undisclosed. In this work, we demonstrate that targeted improvements in model understanding, data quality, and training pipelines, coupled with agentic inference-time scaling, can substantially enhance generation and editing performance even under highly constrained compute budgets. Comprehensive evaluations show that Boogu-Image-0.1 consistently matches or surpasses other open-source models across standard benchmarks, and achieves results approaching leading closed-source systems. Notably, this is accomplished with only 208.62 million unique images. The base model's theoretical training cost is only approximately \$400K. We share practical discussions that we believe are valuable to the broader research community, and release weights, code, and recipes under Apache 2.0 to advance the open ecosystem for unified multimodal understanding and generation. Our code is available here: https://github.com/Boogu-Project/Boogu-Image.

ru.title: Открытая многомодальная модель для генерации и понимания
ru.desc: В этой работе представлен Boogu-Image-0.1 — открытый модуль для многомодального понимания и генерации изображений и текста. Модель демонстрирует высокое качество генерации изображений из текста, быструю инференцию и редактирование на основе инструкций. Кроме того, Boogu-Image-0.1 достигает конкурентоспособных результатов по сравнению с закрытыми системами, используя около 208,62 миллиона уникальных изображений и всего за примерно 400 тысяч долларов на обучение. Мы делимся кодом и весами модели под лицензией Apache 2.0 для поддержки открытого экосистемы многомодального понимания и генерации.

en.title: Unlocking Multimodal Potential with Boogu-Image-0.1
en.desc: Boogu-Image-0.1 is a new open-source model family designed for multimodal understanding and generation, including variants like Base and Turbo. It excels in generating high-quality images from text, performing fast edits, and rendering bilingual text in Chinese and English. The model achieves impressive results by improving understanding, data quality, and training methods, even with limited computational resources. Evaluations show that it competes well with both open-source and closed-source systems, while being accessible to the research community.

papers.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract  Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards without human-annotated data, often referred to as zero RL, has emerged as a powerful paradigm for eliciting chain-of-thought reasoning. However, due to computational constraints, existing studies are largely restricted to small models, leaving the training dynamics and emergent capabilities at a large scale unexplored. To meaningfully explore this frontier, we aim to elicit high-quality reasoning behaviors from the model. However, we find that naive scaling often suffers from poor readability, token redundancy, and a lack of adaptive reasoning depth. To address these challenges, we present a stable and efficient training pipeline, incorporating algorithmic and system optimizations such as clipped importance sampling, training-inference ratio correction, and mixed-precision control. Our experiments offer three key findings that validate the "bitter lesson" of scaling: (1) scaling to 1T parameters significantly enhances sample efficiency and performance ceilings; (2) the training process progresses sequentially through an initial discovery phase followed by a sharpening phase; and (3) the model spontaneously develops advanced cognitive behaviors, including anthropomorphism, structured formatting, self-verification, parallel reasoning, and context anxiety, rendering hand-crafted heuristics redundant. Evaluated on seven mathematical benchmarks, Ring-2.5-1T-Zero achieves competitive performance. Additionally, to assess CoT quality beyond final-answer correctness, we propose a structured evaluation framework across three dimensions: comprehensibility, reproducibility, and efficiency, where our model demonstrates clear advantages in producing structured and concise reasoning traces. By sharing our observed emergent phenomena, we hope to provide the community with deeper insights into scaling behaviors, particularly at the 1-trillion scale.
affiliations: Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China

ru.title: Усиленное обучение без аннотаций: прорыв в масштабах
ru.desc: Статья описывает подход усиленного обучения с проверяемыми вознаграждениями без аннотированных человеком данных, называемым нулевым RL. Исследование фокусируется на масштабировании моделей до 1 триллиона параметров, что позволяет улучшить эффективность образцов и производительность. Авторы представляют стабильный и эффективный процесс обучения с внедрением алгоритмических оптимизаций и системой управления смешанной точностью. Результаты показывают, что модель развивает сложные когнитивные способности, которые делают ручные эвристики избыточными.

en.title: Unlocking Advanced Reasoning with Zero RL at Scale
en.desc: This paper explores reinforcement learning without human-annotated data, known as zero RL, focusing on enhancing reasoning capabilities in large models. The authors identify challenges in scaling, such as poor readability and token redundancy, and propose a stable training pipeline with optimizations like clipped importance sampling. Their findings reveal that scaling to 1 trillion parameters improves sample efficiency and leads to the emergence of advanced cognitive behaviors. The model, Ring-2.5-1T-Zero, shows competitive performance on mathematical benchmarks and excels in structured reasoning evaluation.

papers.title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
papers.abstract: Abstract  OpenClaw has emerged as a leading agent framework for complex task automation, yet it faces insufficient cross-platform GUI interaction support and a well-built self-evolution mechanism. These flaws limit its adaptation to diverse device ecosystems and prevent performance improvements through continuous learning from execution experience. To resolve these issues, we propose the Know Deeply, Act Perfectly paradigm for personal assistants, which holds that accumulated user interaction and task-running experience directly improve execution accuracy and efficiency, unifying cognitive comprehension and operational execution. Based on this paradigm, we introduce KnowAct-GUIClaw, a novel Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework designed to address OpenClaw's GUI manipulation deficits and break through its cross-platform and recursive self-improvement constraints. First, the host agent leverages accumulated interaction experience and task-relevant knowledge for long-horizon task decomposition and allocation (Know). Second, a pluggable GUI subagent with an experience-attributable memory system (Know) and self-evolving skill library (Act), enabling seamless cross-platform migration and fast-path integration. Especially, this framework continuously stores user profiles and feedback to improve the accuracy of task decomposition and tool calls. Extensive experiments across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows show that KnowAct-GUIClaw achieves superior efficiency, accuracy and cross-platform adaptability. Especially, the GUIClaw with open-source Kimi-2.6 models achieves the best performance (64.1%) on the long-horizon MobileWorld benchmark, beating all agentical frameworks and closed-source agentical models, e.g., Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5. Additionally, the knowledgeable memory and execution skills supported by our framework are transferable across diverse base models, improving by 8.5% with Kimi-2.6.

ru.title: Знай Досконально, Действуй Совершенно!
ru.desc: Статья представляет новый подход к автоматизации сложных задач с помощью фреймворка KnowAct-GUIClaw. Он решает проблемы взаимодействия с графическими интерфейсами и самосовершенствования в OpenClaw. Новый метод позволяет усваивать опыт пользователя для повышения точности и эффективности выполнения задач. Эксперименты показывают, что KnowAct-GUIClaw превосходит конкурентов по производительности на различных платформах.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Knowledge and Adaptability
en.desc: The paper introduces KnowAct-GUIClaw, a new framework designed to enhance the OpenClaw agent for better cross-platform GUI interaction and self-evolution. It emphasizes the importance of learning from user interactions to improve task execution accuracy and efficiency. The framework incorporates a memory system and a skill library that evolve based on accumulated experiences, allowing for seamless adaptation across different devices. Experimental results demonstrate that KnowAct-GUIClaw outperforms existing models in efficiency and accuracy, particularly in long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: OvisOCR2 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce OvisOCR2, a 0.8B document parsing model. OvisOCR2 is designed as an end-to-end parser: given a document page image, it generates a Markdown representation in natural reading order, covering text, formulas, tables, and visual regions. We build a data engine that combines filtered real-document annotations with synthetic pages whose rendered images and Markdown targets are derived from the same HTML source. The training recipe includes supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning on a 4B branch with a multi-component reward design, on-policy distillation into the 0.8B model, and model fusion. On OmniDocBench v1.6, OvisOCR2 achieves a state-of-the-art overall score of 96.58, placing an end-to-end model at the top of this leaderboard previously dominated by pipeline methods and highlighting the potential of end-to-end document parsing. On PureDocBench, OvisOCR2 also achieves the highest Avg3 score of 75.06. Beyond these two public benchmarks, we evaluate OvisOCR2 on an in-house benchmark designed to cover a broader set of long-tail and challenging scenarios. OvisOCR2 obtains the best overall performance among the compared methods, providing further evidence of its generalization and robustness. OvisOCR2 is available at https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR2.

ru.title: OvisOCR2: Новая эра парсинга документов
ru.desc: OvisOCR2 — это модель парсинга документов с 0.8 миллиарда параметров. Она работает как конечный парсер, который принимает изображение страницы документа и генерирует представление в формате Markdown. Модель была обучена с использованием смешанных данных, включая реальные аннотации и синтетические страницы, а также использует обучение с подкреплением. OvisOCR2 показывает превосходные результаты на различных бенчмарках, устанавливая новые достижения для end-to-end парсинга документов.

en.title: Revolutionizing Document Parsing with OvisOCR2
en.desc: OvisOCR2 is a document parsing model that processes images of documents and converts them into a structured Markdown format. It uses a combination of real and synthetic data for training, employing techniques like supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to enhance its performance. The model achieves top scores on various benchmarks, outperforming traditional pipeline methods and demonstrating its effectiveness in end-to-end document parsing. Its robust performance across diverse scenarios showcases its ability to generalize well to different types of documents.

papers.title: PolicyShiftGuard: Benchmarking and Improving Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrails
papers.abstract: Abstract  Image guardrails are typically trained and evaluated under a fixed safety policy, implicitly treating safety as an intrinsic property of an image. Real deployments are different: the same image may be allowed in one product, restricted in another, and newly disallowed when a policy boundary changes. We study policy-adaptive image guardrailing, where a model must decide whether an image violates the currently supplied policy and generalize to held-out policy definitions. We introduce PolicyShiftBench, a comprehensive benchmark with 2,000 policy-discriminative instances over 265 images, where each image is paired with 7.55 policy-conditioned prompts on average to test whether models adapt to the active policy rather than relying on image-level safety priors. We then propose PolicyShiftGuard, a compact policy-conditioned guardrail trained with a two-stage training recipe that combines Randomized Policy SFT (RP-SFT) with Boundary-Pair Policy Adaptation (BP-Adapt). BP-Adapt trains matched prompts for the same image and risk category using standard label supervision and a pairwise comparison loss that separates blocking policies from passing policies. Experiments show that existing VLMs and specialized guardrails remain brittle under policy shifts, while PolicyShiftGuard substantially improves policy-sensitive performance. The 7B model achieves SOTA performance of 76.9 Avg. F1 and 72.1 Avg. PSS on PolicyShiftBench, transfers well to UnSafeBench and SafeEditBench, and improves the latency-performance trade-off with a concise output format. Ablations confirm that matched pass/block boundary pairs are essential for stable policy adaptation.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Адаптация охраны изображений к изменяющимся условиям безопасности
ru.desc: В данной статье исследуется проблема адаптации охраны изображений в соответствии с изменяющимися политиками безопасности. Авторы представляют новый бенчмарк PolicyShiftBench, который содержит 2000 случаев, позволяющих оценить, как модели способны адаптироваться к текущим политическим требованиям. Они предлагают метод PolicyShiftGuard, который использует двухступенчатую тренировку для улучшения производительности моделей несмотря на изменения в политике. Эксперименты показывают, что предложенный подход значительно улучшает адаптацию к политическим условиям в сравнении с существующими методами.

en.title: Adapting Image Guardrails to Dynamic Safety Policies
en.desc: This paper addresses the challenge of adapting image guardrails to changing safety policies, which is crucial for real-world applications. It introduces PolicyShiftBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate how well models can adapt to different policy definitions using a diverse set of images and prompts. The authors propose PolicyShiftGuard, a novel guardrail model that employs a two-stage training process to enhance policy-sensitive performance. Experimental results demonstrate that PolicyShiftGuard outperforms existing models in adapting to policy shifts, achieving state-of-the-art results on the benchmark.

papers.title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch
papers.abstract: Abstract  World Action Models (WAMs) improve robot policy learning by jointly modeling actions and future visual observations, using future scene evolution as dense supervision for physically grounded action generation. However, a common design in existing WAMs is to explicitly generate future videos at inference time, incurring substantial computational overhead and hindering real-time closed-loop deployment. GigaWorld-Policy addresses this issue with an action-centered formulation, where future visual dynamics are used during training while action-only decoding is used at inference time. Building upon this framework, we present GigaWorld-Policy-0.5, an enhanced action-centered WAM designed for more efficient robot control. During pretraining, GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 adopts a mixed Action-Conditioned World Modeling (AC-WM) and WAM training strategy. This strengthens the coupling between visual dynamics and robot actions and improves the transferability of action representations for downstream policy learning. For efficient inference, GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 introduces a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that separates visual dynamics modeling and action generation into specialized experts, reducing active computation during action-only inference and achieving 85 ms inference latency on a local RTX 4090 setup. In addition, we employ an agent-based AutoResearch pipeline to systematically search training configurations, enabling more efficient identification of optimal experimental setups while reducing the time and manual intervention required for hyperparameter tuning. Experiments and ablations show that GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 preserves the training benefits of future visual dynamics while improving inference efficiency for robot control.

ru.title: Эффективное управление роботами с помощью GigaWorld-Policy-0.5
ru.desc: Модель GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 улучшает обучение политики роботов, эффективно комбинируя моделирование действий и будущих визуальных наблюдений. В отличие от предыдущих моделей, она использует упрощенное декодирование действий на этапе вывода, что снижает вычислительные затраты и ускоряет процесс. В ходе предварительного обучения применяется смешанная стратегия Action-Conditioned World Modeling и WAM, что укрепляет связь между визуальной динамикой и действиями робота. Также используется архитектура Mixture-of-Transformers, позволяющая снижать задержки при выводе только действий.

en.title: Efficient Robot Control with Action-Centered World Models
en.desc: World Action Models (WAMs) enhance how robots learn to make decisions by predicting future visual outcomes based on their actions. The GigaWorld-Policy approach reduces the computational load during inference by focusing on action-only decoding instead of generating full future videos. GigaWorld-Policy-0.5 further improves this by using a mixed training strategy that strengthens the link between visual dynamics and robot actions. It also employs a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture to optimize inference speed, achieving low latency while maintaining the benefits of future visual dynamics in training.

papers.title: MetaView: Monocular Novel View Synthesis with Scale-Aware Implicit Geometry Priors
papers.abstract: Abstract  Current visual generation models are capable of producing high-quality content, yet they lack a coherent perception of the spatial structure. Existing generative novel view synthesis methods typically introduce explicit geometry priors, which enforce spatial consistency but inherently restrict generalization in large view changes. In contrast, recent interactive generative methods favor implicit scene modeling, offering greater flexibility at the cost of precise camera control and geometry consistency. In this paper, we propose MetaView, a diffusion-based monocular novel view synthesis framework that enables rendering under large view changes from a single image. Our key insight is to combine implicit geometry modeling with minimal yet essential explicit 3D cues: we incorporate implicit geometry priors from a feed-forward geometry perception network to regularize structure without imposing restrictive reconstruction pipelines, while leveraging metric depth to anchor the generation to a metric scale. This design allows MetaView to achieve both geometry consistency and precise controllability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, under challenging monocular large viewpoint changes, MetaView significantly outperforms existing methods and exhibits superior generalization. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/KlingAIResearch/MetaView.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Новый взгляд на генерацию изображений
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен новый подход к синтезу изображений под названием MetaView, который использует диффузионные модели для генерации новых видов с одного изображения. Основная идея заключается в сочетании неявного моделирования геометрии с минимальными явными 3D подсказками, что позволяет достигать согласованности геометрии и точного управления. MetaView демонстрирует высокие результаты при больших изменениях угла обзора, превосходя существующие методы. Эксперименты показывают, что этот подход обеспечивает лучшую обобщаемость и качество синтезируемого контента.

en.title: MetaView: Flexible and Consistent Novel View Synthesis
en.desc: This paper introduces MetaView, a novel framework for generating images from different viewpoints using a single image. It combines implicit geometry modeling with essential explicit 3D cues to maintain spatial consistency while allowing for flexibility in view changes. By using a feed-forward geometry perception network, MetaView regularizes the structure without limiting the reconstruction process. The results show that MetaView outperforms existing methods in generating high-quality images under challenging conditions.

papers.title: Hallo4D: Multi-Modal Hallucination Mitigation for Consistent Spatio-Temporal Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract  While recent advances in 3D generation have enabled impressive visual synthesis, existing methods often rely on 2D diffusion supervision without explicit mechanisms for geometric consistency, leading to spatial hallucinations such as duplicated structures and misaligned geometry. These issues become more severe in 4D generation, where maintaining consistency across viewpoints and temporal evolution introduces additional challenges, including jitter, identity flicker, and structural drift. We present Hallo4D, a unified and model-agnostic framework for mitigating spatiotemporal hallucinations in 3D and 4D content generation. Hallo4D introduces a generation-detection-correction paradigm that leverages large multimodal language models (LMMs) to identify and summarize spatial and temporal inconsistencies from multi-view and multi-frame renderings. These insights guide a consensus-driven image-space consistency optimization, where an LMM-based selector evaluates candidate corrections through multi-model voting, without requiring retraining or architectural modifications. To further improve temporal consistency and optimization efficiency, Hallo4D incorporates motion-aware keyframe sampling, LMM-guided initialization, and appearance alignment. We additionally introduce exposure-aware optimization and visibility pruning to enhance robustness under challenging viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Hallo4D consistently outperforms strong baselines across diverse 3D and 4D generation settings, providing a scalable and generalizable solution for consistency-aware content generation.
affiliations: MAIS&NLPR, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Science, Beijing, 100190, China
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 101408, China

ru.title: Новая эра в генерации 3D и 4D контента
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен метод Hallo4D, который решает проблемы генерирования 3D и 4D контента, связанные с пространственными несоответствиями. Существующие подходы часто используют 2D диффузионное управление без учета геометрической согласованности, что приводит к артефактам, таким как дублирование объектов. Hallo4D внедряет парадигму генерации-обнаружения-исправления, используя большие мультимодальные языковые модели для определения и устранения несоответствий. Эксперименты показывают, что новый метод превосходит существующие решения по различным критериям.

en.title: Enhancing Consistency in 3D and 4D Generation with Hallo4D
en.desc: This paper presents Hallo4D, a framework designed to improve the consistency of 3D and 4D content generation. It addresses issues like spatial hallucinations and temporal inconsistencies that arise from using 2D diffusion supervision. By employing a generation-detection-correction approach, it utilizes large multimodal language models to identify and correct inconsistencies in generated content. The framework enhances optimization efficiency and robustness through techniques like motion-aware keyframe sampling and exposure-aware optimization.

papers.title: Registers Matter for Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Abstract  Vision Transformers (ViTs) are known to exhibit high-norm patch-token outliers that degrade feature map quality, a problem effectively mitigated by register tokens. As diffusion models increasingly adopt transformer architectures and move toward pixel-space training, they become closer in form to ViTs, raising the question of whether register tokens are also useful for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs). In this work, we show that DiTs differ from ViTs in a key respect: they do not exhibit patch-token outliers but still benefit from registers. Interestingly, registers are more effective in pixel-space DiTs than in latent-space DiTs. By analyzing intermediate representations, we find that register tokens produce cleaner feature maps at high noise levels, which may contribute to their effectiveness in pixel-space generation. We further observe that recent pixel-space DiT architectures implicitly incorporate register-like mechanisms, which may partially account for their strong empirical performance. Motivated by these observations, we propose Register Guidance, a technique that amplifies the contribution of register tokens responsible for improving visual structure and coherence.

ru.title: Улучшение генерации изображений с помощью токенов регистрации
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматриваются Vision Transformers (ViTs) и их проблема с аномальными токенами, которые ухудшают качество признаковых карт. Авторы показывают, что Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) не имеют таких аномалий, но все же выигрывают от использования токенов регистрации. Интересно, что в DiTs, работающих в пиксельном пространстве, токены регистрации оказывают большее влияние, чем в скрытом пространстве. В заключение, предложена техника Register Guidance для улучшения визуальной структуры и согласованности на основе токенов регистрации.

en.title: Enhancing Diffusion Transformers with Register Guidance
en.desc: This paper investigates the role of register tokens in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) and compares them to Vision Transformers (ViTs). While DiTs do not have the same patch-token outliers that ViTs do, they still benefit from the use of register tokens, especially in pixel-space training. The authors find that register tokens help produce cleaner feature maps under high noise conditions, enhancing the quality of generated images. They introduce a technique called Register Guidance to further improve visual structure and coherence in DiTs.

papers.title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Structured pruning is a hardware-friendly way to compress LLMs, but it is mostly validated on multiple-choice recognition tasks, while the same compressed checkpoints can collapse on the free-form generation that deployment actually requires. Two observations trace this gap. First, greedy pass@1 nearly vanishes after compression, yet pass@k recovers substantially under repeated sampling: useful generations are demoted, not erased. Second, the recoverable regime fails mainly through suffix repetition. Recovery should therefore train on the compressed model's own on-policy states with dense token-level supervision, which On-Policy Distillation (OPD) provides by reusing the pre-compression model as a frozen teacher. However, long on-policy rollouts spend early recovery budget on low-information repetitive suffixes, delaying loss descent. To mitigate this waste, we propose \shortopd, a short-to-long OPD schedule that detects teacher-confirmed repetitive suffixes, treats the surviving prefix as each rollout's effective length, and allocates future rollout budgets to the effective lengths the policy can currently use. Across math, code, and open-ended generation, \shortopd\ raises the compressed model's score to about 9times its unrecovered value and 1.6--4.4times standard recovery recipes (SFT w/o KD, KD, and SeqKD), and it matches a fixed 8192-token rollout horizon within two points using a quarter of the training time (8.5 vs.\ 35.9 hours) and 71% fewer rollout tokens. We hope this recipe helps move structured pruning beyond marginal gains on perplexity and multiple-choice benchmarks, a step closer to deployment-ready generation quality.
affiliations: Chinese Information Processing Laboratory, Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Оптимизация сжатия для качественного генерации
ru.desc: Структурная обрезка является удобным способом сжатия больших языковых моделей (LLM), но в основном она проверялась только на задачах выбора из нескольких вариантов. В данной работе выявлены две проблемы: первая заключается в том, что после сжатия результат pass@1 значительно снижается, но pass@k восстанавливается при повторном образце. Вторая проблема - это повторение суффиксов. Для решения этой проблемы мы предлагаем метод короткой-до-длинной дистилляции, который эффективно управляет обучением сжатой модели на основе собственных состояний и уменьшает ненужные затраты на восстановление.

en.title: Optimizing Compressed LLMs for Better Generation Quality
en.desc: This paper discusses structured pruning as a method to compress large language models (LLMs) for better efficiency. It identifies that while traditional evaluation methods show a drop in performance after compression, useful outputs can still be generated through repeated sampling. The authors propose On-Policy Distillation (OPD) to improve recovery by training on the compressed model's outputs, but highlight issues with repetitive suffixes wasting recovery resources. To address this, they introduce a short-to-long OPD schedule that optimizes the training process, resulting in significant performance improvements across various tasks.

papers.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
papers.abstract: Abstract  Self-improving autonomous agents are moving from research prototypes to deployed systems. The primary goal is controllable evolution, or adaptation, from experience with minimal or even no human input. This survey frames modern self-improving agents as adaptive systems that convert experience into accumulated capability gains. We offer a system-level framework that represents a modern agent as a configuration coupling a foundation model with an operational scaffold of prompts, memory, tools, and control logic. Within this framework, self-improvement is formalized as a self-induced update operator that obtains and commits updates to model parameters or scaffold components. We organize prior work by update target and by the signals that drive change, then review applications and discuss evaluation, before closing with open problems and future directions. For convenience, we track technical updates on https://github.com/selfimproving-agent/awesome-Self-Improving-Agents.
affiliations: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
School of Artificial Intelligence, Jilin University

ru.title: Автономные агенты: эволюция без человека
ru.desc: В этой статье рассматриваются автономные агенты, которые самостоятельно улучшают свои способности. Основная цель таких агентов — контролируемая эволюция и адаптация на основе опыта с минимальным или отсутствием вмешательства человека. Исследуется система, в которой агенты используют модели, подсказки, память, инструменты и логику управления для самосовершенствования. Обсуждаются предыдущие работы, приложения, методы оценки, а также открытые вопросы для будущих исследований.

en.title: Empowering Agents: Evolving Autonomy Through Experience
en.desc: This paper discusses the development of self-improving autonomous agents that can adapt and evolve with little to no human intervention. It presents a framework that combines a foundation model with various components like prompts, memory, and control logic to facilitate this adaptation. The authors formalize self-improvement as a process where agents update their model parameters or components based on their experiences. The paper also categorizes previous research by the targets of updates and the signals that prompt changes, while highlighting applications, evaluation methods, and future research directions.

papers.title: Vinci2: Providing Proactive Assistance in Continuous Egocentric Videos
papers.abstract: Abstract  When should an intelligent assistant speak up without being asked? Continuous egocentric video offers rich, evolving context that enables a new form of assistance: one that is proactive rather than merely reactive. Yet existing approaches either wait passively for user queries or treat every detected event as requiring a response, without considering the user's history, current activity, or whether assistance would actually be welcome. We reframe proactive assistance as a context-dependent decision problem: the agent must not only perceive what is happening, but reason over accumulated temporal context to determine when and whether to intervene. To this end, we present Vinci2, a proactive egocentric assistance system that advances the on-device assistant Vinci from reactive response toward proactivity. On the evaluation side, we present EgoServe, the first large-scale benchmark for proactive assistance in continuous egocentric video. EgoServe comprises over 3,000 service instances organized along 4 temporal memory horizons, ranging from immediate safety alerts to long-term habit coaching, across 10 service categories. On the modeling side, we propose EgoMemo, a training-free, memory-augmented agent that maintains three complementary memory representations: multi-scale temporal summaries, a semantic knowledge graph, and visual embedding archives. At each timestep, EgoMemo performs retrieval-augmented reasoning to determine whether assistance is warranted and, if so, produces contextually grounded responses. Experiments demonstrate that EgoMemo establishes strong baselines on EgoServe while remaining competitive on existing egocentric benchmarks. Our benchmark and code are publicly available at https://sitonggong.github.io/EgoServe-page/{Vinci2}.

ru.title: Интеллектуальный помощник: проактивный, а не реактивный
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается необходимость проактивного поведения интеллектуального помощника, который должен реагировать на события без явного запроса пользователя. Проблема проактивного помощника переосмысляется как задача, зависящая от контекста, где необходимо учитывать историю пользователя и текущую активность. Представлен новый подход с использованием системы Vinci2, которая использует видео с эгоцентрической точки зрения для проактивной помощи. Также представлен EgoServe, первый крупномасштабный бенчмарк, который позволяет оценить эффективность проактивной помощи в контексте эгоцентрического видео.

en.title: Proactive Assistance: Anticipating User Needs with Vinci2
en.desc: This paper introduces Vinci2, a proactive egocentric assistance system that enhances user interaction by anticipating needs rather than just reacting to requests. It addresses the limitations of existing systems that either wait for user input or respond to every detected event without considering context. The authors propose EgoMemo, a memory-augmented agent that uses multiple memory representations to make informed decisions about when to provide assistance. They also present EgoServe, a large-scale benchmark for evaluating proactive assistance in continuous egocentric video, demonstrating that their approach outperforms existing methods.

papers.title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities
papers.abstract: Abstract  As Large Language Models (LLMs) evolve into autonomous agents, the need for unified evaluation infrastructure becomes critical. However, current evaluation pipelines remain highly fragmented and tightly coupled, hindering reproducibility and causing redundant engineering. To address this, we introduce AgentCompass, an open-source, lightweight, and extensible infrastructure for evaluating LLM-based agents. AgentCompass organizes the evaluation process around three independent components, namely Benchmark, Harness, and Environment, thereby enabling flexible configurations without requiring the reimplementation of complex execution logic. Furthermore, it features a fault-tolerant asynchronous runtime and comprehensive trajectory analysis tools to transparently diagnose nuanced failure modes like reward-hacking. Natively supporting over 20 benchmarks across five capability dimensions, AgentCompass provides the community with a scalable and reproducible infrastructure for advancing agent research.

ru.title: Новая эра оценки агентов на базе LLM
ru.desc: Статья представляет новый инструмент под названием AgentCompass, который помогает в оценке автономных агентов на основе LLM. Он решает проблему фрагментации существующих методов оценки и упрощает процесс благодаря трем независимым компонентам: Benchmark, Harness и Environment. AgentCompass позволяет гибко конфигурировать оценку без лишней переработки логики выполнения и предоставляет инструменты для анализа ошибок. Этот инструмент поддерживает более 20 бенчмарков и обеспечивает сообществу масштабируемую инфраструктуру для исследований в области агентов.

en.title: Streamlining Evaluation for LLM Agents with AgentCompass
en.desc: This paper presents AgentCompass, a new framework designed to evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) agents effectively. It addresses the issues of fragmented evaluation processes by organizing them into three independent components: Benchmark, Harness, and Environment. This structure allows for flexible configurations and enhances reproducibility without the need for complex reimplementation. Additionally, AgentCompass includes tools for diagnosing failure modes and supports over 20 benchmarks, making it a valuable resource for advancing research in autonomous agents.

papers.title: Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success
papers.abstract: Abstract  Failure attribution for LLM-based agentic systems, i.e., identifying which steps in a failure trajectory caused the task to fail, is critical for debugging and improving these systems. Existing approaches either rely on prompting-based pipelines, which are computationally expensive, or require post-training on failure trajectories with step-level error annotations, which are costly to collect and difficult to scale. We argue that a practical failure attribution model should be lightweight and trainable without step-level supervision on failure data. To this end, we address unsupervised failure attribution, i.e., training exclusively on successful trajectories and identifying error steps at inference time given a failure trajectory. We propose OAT, which casts this problem as one-class learning with neural controlled differential equations, modeling the dynamical pattern of successful trajectories in latent space. At inference time, each step in a failure trajectory is assigned an anomaly score based on its deviation from the dynamics learned on successful trajectories, which is then used to form a set of error steps. With training on only 100 successful trajectories, experiments show that OAT is 200--5000 times faster than prompting-based baselines, and, at the same time, consistently outperforms them in both in-domain and out-of-distribution datasets with +20% and +7% F1 scores, respectively, demonstrating that OAT is a promising and efficient direction for diagnosing agentic system failures.
affiliations: Department of Computer Science, University of Wisconsin-Madison

ru.title: Эффективная диагностика сбоев в LLM-системах
ru.desc: Статья посвящена выявлению причин сбоя в системах, основанных на LLM, что критично для их отладки и улучшения. Авторы предлагают новый подход, который не требует затратных аннотаций и может тренироваться только на успешных траекториях. Метод OAT использует одноклассное обучение, чтобы моделировать успешные сценарии и выявлять ошибочные шаги в процессе работы системы. Результаты показывают, что OAT значительно быстрее существующих методов и превосходит их по метрикам качества.

en.title: Efficient Failure Diagnosis for LLMs with OAT
en.desc: This paper presents a method for identifying the causes of failures in large language model (LLM)-based systems, which is essential for debugging. The proposed approach, called OAT, focuses on unsupervised failure attribution, allowing the model to learn from successful task trajectories without needing detailed error annotations. By using one-class learning with neural controlled differential equations, OAT efficiently detects anomalies in failure trajectories based on learned patterns from successful ones. The results show that OAT is significantly faster and more effective than existing methods, making it a valuable tool for improving agentic systems.

papers.title: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs) have recently emerged as a compelling alternative to autoregressive (AR) modeling for discrete data, offering parallel generation and iterative global refinement capabilities. Unlike continuous diffusion, where the state space is fixed, DDMs are fundamentally shaped by how the discrete state space is constructed: the tokenization scheme, the vocabulary topology, and domain-specific structural alphabets. This work introduces a unified conceptual framework that views discrete diffusion models through the construction of the underlying discrete state space. Within this framework, existing formulations, including transition-matrix, masking/absorbing-state, and score/ratio-based approaches, emerge as different instantiations of a common design space. The framework further exposes common design trade-offs across training objectives, inference algorithms, scaling behavior, systems optimization, and evaluation protocols, suggesting several promising directions for future research.
affiliations: MBZUAI - Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

ru.title: Новые горизонты в дискретной диффузии
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматриваются дискретные модели диффузии для устранения шумов (DDMs) как альтернатива автогрессивному моделированию для дискретных данных. Главное внимание уделяется тому, как построение дискретного пространства состояний влияет на эффективность этих моделей. Предлагается единая концептуальная рамка, которая объединяет различные подходы к моделям диффузии, позволяя лучше понимать их взаимодействие и применение. Также обсуждаются важные компромиссы в проектировании, методы обучения и алгоритмы вывода, открывающие новые направления для будущих исследований.

en.title: Revolutionizing Discrete Data Generation with Denoising Diffusion Models
en.desc: This paper discusses discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs) as a new approach for generating discrete data, which can perform better than traditional autoregressive models. It emphasizes the importance of how the discrete state space is designed, including aspects like tokenization and vocabulary structure. The authors present a unified framework that connects various existing methods of DDMs, showing they are different versions of a similar concept. Additionally, the framework highlights key trade-offs in training, inference, and evaluation, paving the way for future advancements in this area.

papers.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract  The optimization of long-horizon agents increasingly relies on reflection-based mechanisms, where a large language model (LLM) acts as an optimizer to diagnose agent failures and improve agent policies. However, real execution traces are difficult to use directly for optimization: large trace collections are often redundant and heterogeneous, making optimization inefficient and prone to overfitting to low-value failures; meanwhile, each individual trajectory also contains many irrelevant steps, while naive context reduction methods such as truncation or sliding windows can discard causally important evidence and produce misleading optimization signals. To resolve this dilemma, we introduce STRACE (Structural TRajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction), a framework that constructs high signal-noise optimization contexts for more precise and effective optimization. At the batch level, STRACE mines failure patterns to filter redundant traces and retain representative failures; within each selected trace, it performs causal localization over a textual dependency graph to remove non-causal steps and identify the true root-cause module for optimization. Empirical results demonstrate that STRACE significantly outperforms standard context-filtering baselines. Notably, on a challenging formal verification task (VeruSAGE-Bench), it successfully optimizes human-expert designed agents, delivering 1.4times success-rate improvement (42.5% to 58.5%). The code is available at https://github.com/moomight/STRACE .
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China

ru.title: Оптимизация агентов с помощью STRACE
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматривается оптимизация агентов с длинным горизонтом, использующих рефлексивные механизмы и большие языковые модели (LLM) для выявления ошибок и улучшения политик агентов. Проблема заключается в том, что реальные траектории выполнения часто содержат избыточные и неоднородные данные, что делает оптимизацию неэффективной. Авторы предлагают новый фреймворк STRACE, который анализирует траектории и извлекает причинные данные для более точной оптимизации. Результаты экспериментов показывают, что STRACE значительно превосходит стандартные методы фильтрации контекста и улучшает успех оптимизации агентов экспертов.

en.title: Optimizing Agents with Causal Insights
en.desc: This paper presents STRACE, a framework designed to optimize long-horizon agents using reflection-based mechanisms with large language models. STRACE addresses the challenges of using real execution traces for optimization by filtering out redundant and irrelevant steps, ensuring that only high-value failures are retained. It employs causal localization to identify the root causes of failures, enhancing the optimization process. Empirical results show that STRACE significantly improves the success rate of agent optimization tasks compared to standard methods.

papers.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large Language Model (LLM) agents have moved beyond generating responses to executing multi-step tasks by calling tools, observing the results, and iteratively deciding the next action. Most agent systems run on desktops or servers, which support tool use and task automation. Mobile devices are also important agent environments because they are widely accessible and contain users' data, sensors, and daily-use applications. Existing mobile agents mainly operate smartphones through graphical user interface (GUI) actions such as tapping, swiping, and typing, which often form long, interface-dependent sequences, cannot directly access device capabilities, and make execution boundaries difficult to define. We present PalmClaw, an open-source agent framework that runs natively on mobile phones and manages the sessions, memory, skills, tools, and agent loop directly on the device. PalmClaw exposes device capabilities as device tools with explicit arguments, structured results, and clearly defined execution boundaries. This design enables agents to use mobile capabilities directly while keeping each action explicit and controlled. Experiments show an 11.5\% relative improvement in task success and a 94.9\% reduction in completion time over the strongest baseline, with lower setup burden and traces illustrating how execution boundaries are applied. Code is available at https://github.com/ModalityDance/PalmClaw.

ru.title: Эффективные мобильные агенты с PalmClaw
ru.desc: Статья представляет новый фреймворк PalmClaw, который позволяет агентам на мобильных устройствах выполнять многоступенчатые задачи прямо на телефоне. Он управляет сессиями, памятью и инструментами, обеспечивая четкое определение границ выполнения. PalmClaw использует возможности устройства в виде явных инструментов с заданными аргументами и структурированными результатами, что повышает контроль над действиями агента. Испытания показали значительное улучшение успеха выполнения задач и сокращение времени завершения по сравнению с существующими системами.

en.title: Empowering Mobile Agents with Direct Device Access
en.desc: The paper introduces PalmClaw, an open-source framework designed for Large Language Model (LLM) agents to operate natively on mobile devices. Unlike existing mobile agents that rely on graphical user interface actions, PalmClaw allows agents to directly access device capabilities with clearly defined execution boundaries. This approach enhances task automation by managing sessions, memory, skills, and tools directly on the device. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates and reduced completion times compared to previous systems.

papers.title: Self in Space: Benchmarking Self-Awareness and Spatial Cognition in UAV Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract  Autonomous UAV systems increasingly rely on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to operate in complex real-world environments. Such embodied scenarios require not only understanding the surrounding space but also maintaining a coherent representation of the agent itself. However, existing UAV-oriented approaches and benchmarks remain largely environment-centric, primarily focusing on spatial understanding tasks, with the agent's self-awareness remaining implicit. To address this gap, we introduce SIS-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating embodied spatial intelligence in UAV scenarios under a unified self-in-space formulation. SIS-Bench organizes evaluation along two complementary dimensions, space and self, and a three-level hierarchy of perception, memory, and reasoning. It contains 4,856 question--answer pairs across 13 tasks derived from 1,646 real-world UAV videos through a task-conditioned construction pipeline with expert verification.Extensive evaluations reveal that current MLLMs exhibit fundamental limitations in modeling dynamic and agent-centered processes. In particular, we observe a clear imbalance between spatial cognition and self-awareness, as well as a progressive performance degradation across cognitive levels.Motivated by these findings, we further explore a motion-aware representation that incorporates self-related dynamics through optical flow and visual feature fusion. Experimental results show that modeling agent motion consistently improves perception and memory performance, not only in spatial cognition but also in self-awareness, and generalizes to downstream UAV decision-making tasks.Our results highlight the importance of self-awareness for advancing embodied spatial intelligence, and provide both a new benchmark and empirical evidence for motion-aware self-in-space modeling.
affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

ru.title: Сопряжение пространственного интеллекта и осознания себя в БПЛА
ru.desc: Автономные беспилотные летательные аппараты (БПЛА) все чаще используют мультимодальные модели больших языков (MLLM) для работы в сложных реальных условиях. В данной работе представлен новый бенчмарк SIS-Bench, который оценивает пространственный интеллект БПЛА, учитывая как восприятие окружающего мира, так и осознание собственного состояния. Исследования показали, что текущее поколение MLLM имеет значительные ограничения в моделировании динамических и агент-ориентированных процессов. Мы также выяснили, что учитывание динамики движения агента улучшает как восприятие, так и память, что критически важно для принятия решений БПЛА.

en.title: Enhancing UAV Intelligence with Self-Awareness
en.desc: This paper introduces SIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the spatial intelligence of autonomous UAV systems using multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It emphasizes the need for UAVs to not only understand their environment but also maintain self-awareness, which has been overlooked in existing approaches. The benchmark assesses performance across two dimensions: spatial understanding and self-awareness, organized into perception, memory, and reasoning tasks. Experimental results indicate that incorporating motion-aware representations significantly enhances both spatial cognition and self-awareness in UAV decision-making tasks.

papers.title: From Controlled to the Wild: Evaluation of Pentesting Agents for the Real-World
papers.abstract: Abstract  AI pentesting agents are increasingly credible as offensive security systems, but current benchmarks still provide limited guidance on which will perform best in real-world targets. Existing evaluation protocols assess and optimize for predefined goals such as capture-the-flag, remote code execution, exploit reproduction, or trajectory similarity, in simplified or narrow settings. These tools are valuable for measuring bounded capabilities, yet they do not adequately capture the complexity, open-ended exploration, and strategic decision-making required in realistic pentesting. In this paper, we present a practical evaluation protocol that shifts assessment from task completion to validated vulnerability discovery, allowing evaluation in sufficiently complex targets spanning multiple attack surfaces and vulnerability classes. The protocol combines structured ground-truth with LLM-based semantic matching to identify vulnerabilities, bipartite resolution to score findings under realistic ambiguity, continuous ground-truth maintenance, repeated and cumulative evaluation of stochastic agents, efficiency metrics, and reduced-suite selection for sustainable experimentation. This protocol extends the state of the art by enabling a more realistic, operationally informative comparison of AI pentesting agents. To enable reproducibility, we also release expert-annotated ground truth and code for the proposed evaluation protocol: https://github.com/ethiack/ethibench.
affiliations: University of Notre Dame Notre Dame, Indiana, USA

ru.title: Новый подход к оценке агентов AI для пентестинга
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматриваются агенты искусственного интеллекта для пентестинга, которые становятся более надежными в роли атакующих систем безопасности. Авторы предлагают новый протокол оценки, который позволяет лучше оценить способности агентов в обнаружении уязвимостей в сложных целевых системах. Протокол сочетает в себе структурированные данные и семантическое сопоставление на основе LLM для определения уязвимостей с учетом неопределенности. Благодаря этому новому подходу, исследователи могут проводить более реалистичное сравнение агентов AI для пентестинга.

en.title: Revolutionizing AI Pentesting Evaluation for Real-World Effectiveness
en.desc: This paper introduces a new evaluation protocol for AI pentesting agents that focuses on validated vulnerability discovery rather than just task completion. It addresses the limitations of current benchmarks by incorporating complex targets and multiple attack surfaces. The protocol utilizes structured ground-truth and LLM-based semantic matching to enhance vulnerability identification. By providing a more realistic assessment framework, this work aims to improve the comparison and effectiveness of AI-driven security systems in real-world scenarios.

papers.title: AffectFlow-DINO: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Task Affect Estimation via Conditional Rectified Flow
papers.abstract: Abstract  We present AffectFlow-DINO, a multi-task learning system for the 11th ABAW challenge that extends a standard deterministic architecture with a conditional rectified-flow head to model the inherent ambiguity of in-the-wild facial behavior. Instead of predicting a single affect estimate, the model learns a conditional generative distribution, enabling uncertainty-aware one-to-many predictions through Monte Carlo sampling. The system jointly estimates continuous valence-arousal, classifies eight facial expressions, and detects twelve Action Units from static face images. Built on a frozen DINOv3 ViT-S/16 backbone, extensive ablation studies show that rectified-flow decoding consistently improves deterministic prediction, particularly for valence-arousal estimation (CCC-V +0.058). We further show that post-hoc threshold calibration effectively recovers performance on severely imbalanced rare classes (e.g., Fear: 3.8% rightarrow 33.1%) without retraining. Combined with backbone fine-tuning and flow retuning, the final model achieves P_{MTL=1.177}, substantially outperforming the official challenge baseline of P_{MTL}=0.45.
affiliations: Department of Innovation Engineering, University of Salento & Institute of Applied Sciences and Intelligent Systems (CNR), Italy
Faculty of Data Science and Computing, Universiti Malaysia Kelantan, Malaysia
University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU), Spain

ru.title: Многозадачное обучение для анализа лицевых эмоций
ru.desc: В статье представлена система многозадачного обучения AffectFlow-DINO для 11-го конкурса ABAW. Она использует условную архитектуру rectified-flow для моделирования неясности в лицевом поведении. Модель обучается на генеративном распределении, что позволяет делать предсказания с учетом неопределенности. Также система совместно оценивает непрерывные валентность и арousal, классифицирует восемь выражений лиц и определяет двенадцать Action Units.

en.title: Uncertainty-Aware Facial Emotion Recognition
en.desc: AffectFlow-DINO is a multi-task learning system designed for the 11th ABAW challenge, which enhances a standard architecture by incorporating a conditional rectified-flow head. This allows the model to handle the uncertainty in facial expressions by generating a range of possible outcomes instead of a single prediction. It simultaneously estimates continuous valence-arousal, classifies eight facial expressions, and detects twelve Action Units from static images. The model shows significant improvements in performance, particularly in valence-arousal estimation, and effectively addresses class imbalance through post-hoc calibration without needing retraining.
